sections.title: Compare the four reversals before choosing a rule
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The upright images do not supply one reversal rule for all four cards. Waite’s main entries give four different directions. The middle column below paraphrases those historical entries; the final column offers our own questions for the hypothetical reading group above.

Check the entries for [Wands](https://sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktwa04.htm), [Cups](https://sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu04.htm), [Swords](https://sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktsw04.htm) and [Pentacles](https://sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktpe04.htm). These are Waite’s particular divinatory meanings. The practical questions are contemporary reflective applications, not translations of his text or evidence that an event will occur.

headings: A question for the reading group
rows: The favourable sense continues: flourishing, growth, happiness and beauty remain.
Which shared arrangement already works well enough to keep as we expand?
Something new, a sign of what may come, fresh teaching and new connections.
Is there a specific new format or collaborator worth trying, and do members want it?
Sound management, careful judgement and thrift, alongside miserliness, safeguards and a will.
What needs a careful review of costs and responsibilities before we change the schedule?
An unresolved state, postponement or resistance.
Which approval, payment or objection, if any, is actually holding up expansion?

sections.title: Give a reversed Four a question and a job
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The Four of Wands is a useful check on automatic opposites: Waite keeps its favourable direction when reversed. The Four of Swords is a check on selective reading: its list contains both prudent management and miserliness. Keep the awkward terms visible instead of polishing the whole entry into reassurance. Likewise, imagining coins falling from an inverted Four of Pentacles is a possible modern image exercise; it does not make “letting go” Waite’s reversed meaning.

**Original hypothetical variation.** Return to the reading group. There are twelve interested members, the current room seats eight, and the venue has not confirmed a larger room or its fee. Two organisers are available to host. Ask: “What do we need to settle before inviting more members next month?” Arrange the Four of Pentacles reversed yourself; this is a comparison exercise, not a reported draw.

First give the card the position “What remains unsettled?” Using Waite’s delay or resistance as a starting point, propose that the room booking may be the obstacle. That is a hypothesis tied to a known gap. The card cannot tell you that a particular organiser is secretly opposed, how long a delay will last, or whether a fee will rise. Ask the venue about availability, cost and the date by which it can confirm.

Now move the same card to “My next action,” keeping the question and facts unchanged. The interpretation needs to become an action: request those details and agree with the organisers when to decide whether to expand. “Keep waiting” leaves the relevant uncertainty unresolved. Moving the card does not provide a second independent confirmation; you are testing how the position changes the use of one interpretation.

If the venue has already confirmed everything, the booking hypothesis does not fit. Ask which fact remains unknown, or set that interpretation aside if none does. Do not invent an opponent to rescue the word “resistance.” If only the room is available but the fee is still pending, identify that narrower gap. The useful result is a better question about actual arrangements, rather than a claim that the reversed card exposed a hidden cause.

You can do this comparison with a physical deck or the four card images above. For a separate shuffled practice, open the [tarot table](/tarot), decide whether to include reversals before shuffling, and record the card and orientation actually displayed. A shuffled draw is not a preset of these four cards; use whichever card appears rather than repeatedly drawing to force the example. Consult the [card atlas](/journal/tarot-cards) for the image and explain whether you are following a historical entry or trying a modern reflective interpretation.
